_comment: Copy to identity.local.json, which is gitignored, and fill in your own details.
These are deliberately not in criteria.mjs. That file is committed and this skill's
directory is excluded from every scan, so a name or a work domain written there would
be published and invisible to the audit at the same time. A check that greps for an
email address must not ship the email address.
allowedEmails    the addresses a commit may be authored or committed by. Anything
else fails B2 and S4. With this list empty, both report N-A rather
than passing: the audit cannot guess whose repository this is.
forbiddenDomains domains that are definitely wrong for a personal release, such as
an employer's. Regex source, so escape the dots.
patterns         extra things to treat as personal data wherever they appear: your
real name, usernames, a work domain, machine-specific folder names.
allow            matches that are supposed to be there - the name on the copyright
line B6 requires, a published account slug, your own repository's
URL in a clone command. Publishing a repo publishes the username in
its URL; that is not a leak. Keep this narrow all the same.
